intent: Move the must() DOM narrowing helper out of DropZone.test.tsx, which the eslint pass had pushed 6 lines over the 250-line cap, into the shared coverage-excluded test directory where both component tests can use it.
scope: DropZone.test.tsx 256 -> 243 lines; PuzzleResult.test.tsx switched to the shared helper
Non-goal: no behaviour change, no assertion weakened
changes: Extracted must() into src/test/domQueries.ts. That directory is excluded by the coverage config, which is why fixtures already live there - a helper beside a component would be counted as production code and break the 100% gate.
DropZone.test.tsx imports it instead of defining it, dropping the file back under the cap.
PuzzleResult.test.tsx replaced its inline instanceof guard with the same helper, so the two component tests narrow DOM queries identically rather than each rolling their own.

verification.evidence: 40 over-cap files before this change, 39 after; DropZone.test.tsx no longer appears. It had been 250 exactly and the must() helper pushed it to 256, so the eslint commit had silently added an over-cap file while removing others - this restores the intended 41 -> 39 for the session.

100% on all four measures with totals unchanged at 579 statements / 217 branches / 98 functions / 530 lines, and 145 tests in 15 files. Identical totals are the check that moving the helper into a coverage-excluded directory neither removed code from test reach nor added any.
tsc exit 0; eslint still reports exactly the 4 known remaining errors, so the move introduced none.

risks: src/test/domQueries.ts is not coverage-measured, so a bug in must() would not be caught by the coverage gate. It is four lines with a single instanceof check, and every caller exercises it on the happy path in tests that assert on the returned element.
rollback: git revert the commit. must() returns to DropZone.test.tsx and that file goes back over the cap at 256 lines; PuzzleResult.test.tsx regains its inline guard.
After rollback, confirm npm run coverage still reports 100% with 579/217/98/530 and 145 passing tests.
